problem: Can the historical c/k immediately preceding -(a)meke in Steffel's color words be related to the independently attested stative -ga and to the modern color modifiers -ka/-ga?
direct_answer: The continuity hypothesis is now strongly supported at the morphological-system level, although identification of the c/k in each individual historical color lexeme remains unproven.

new_evidence_since_v1.finding: Merrill lists -ga~-ja as an explicit stative suffix, always attested with -(a)meke, and analyzes chains such as -rúgameke as -ru + -ga + -(a)me + -ke.

Steffel treated C/G and K/Q/G among his 'equivocal letters'; Merrill establishes c/k as [k] and documents genuine k~g alternation in addition to contrast. For schiógameke, Merrill explicitly says -gameke could be a variant of the -cameke found in all other basic colors.
The 1997 Compendio explicitly segments sa'p-é-ga-me as flesh-have-state-PARTICIPLE, demonstrating modern -ga + -me outside the color lexemes under audit.
The Compendio groups -ka/-ga/-cha as 'subido' and -ame/-me as participial; it directly attests color forms such as sawaró-ga-me, elamú-ga-me and roso-bó-cha-ga-me.
Baja-TB uses -ga 'continuative/state' productively in color appearance predicates: sejtána-g-ili, siyóna-g-ili, chóna-g-ili, rosóna-g-ili, ulána-g-ili and others.

hypotheses.label: Inherited stative/participial morphology retained and specialized in the color system
hypotheses.mechanism: An older stative -ga plus participial -ame(+ke) domain persisted. Across varieties, velar realizations and later analogical organization yielded modern color patterns in -ka/-ga before participial -me/-mi, while -na developed/retained a contrasting lower-or-becoming color function.
support: Proto-Tarahumara *-ame and pre-Steffel gamek provide historical depth.
Merrill explicitly proposes that -gameke may be a variant of color -cameke given g/c alternation.
Modern multivariety grammar directly attests -ga + -me and productive color-state -ga.
Modern color grammar groups -ka/-ga/-cha functionally and contrasts them with -na.
Independent historical-modern -na bridge shows the color system preserves older verbal/stative morphology beyond the -ame chain.
problems: Black, white and red historical -cameke forms are not individually segmented by Merrill as root + -ga + -ame + -ke.
Steffel's k~g alternation is real but not automatic; minimal contrasts also exist.
The chronology of specialization from general stative morphology to the modern color-degree opposition is not directly dated.

hypotheses.label: Direct retention of older ga+ame(+ke) morphology
hypotheses.mechanism: Historical color -cameke/-gameke broadly continues older stative/participial morphology, but the modern -ka/-na semantic organization cannot yet be reconstructed in detail.

hypotheses.label: Later reanalysis of an inherited opaque -kame(ke) string
hypotheses.mechanism: An inherited chain was later resegmented as modern -ka/-ga + -me.
hypotheses.reason_for_downgrade: Explicit historical -ga+-(a)me+-ke and explicit modern -ga+-me/color-state -ga make a purely late reanalysis less economical, though local reanalysis and analogical remodeling remain possible.

revised_assessment.reason: The same stative + participial architecture is explicitly present in historical and modern sources, and the historical g/c/k alternation plus Merrill's own -gameke~-cameke proposal creates a controlled bridge. The remaining uncertainty is lexeme-specific segmentation and chronology of color specialization, not existence of the ga+ame architecture itself.

epistemic_rule: System-level morphological continuity may be strongly demonstrated while individual lexical segmentation remains uncertain. Do not promote the former into automatic segmentation of every historical color word.
next_tests: Build a targeted historical-modern k~g/ga~ka correspondence series in morphologically comparable environments.
Locate earlier twentieth-century descriptions to date when color -ka/-ga versus -na semantics became explicit.
Search Steffel's accessible lexical material for color or adjectival forms where -ga is independently separable from the root.
Retain direct audit of the unpublished 1799 grammar as a future documentary priority.
